translate_en|mods/JeevesClaims/42/media/: Admins, moderators, and GMs can claim safehouses without waiting for the reclaim cooldown.

The master switch for animal claims. ON by default. Off, and no animal of any kind can be claimed - the Animals tab stays empty, the claim option does not appear, and none of the protections apply. The two switches below decide which animals are included and both also start on, so out of the box every animal is claimable. A claimed animal cannot be killed through the menu, picked up, leashed, tethered, lured, penned, loaded into a trailer, milked, sheared, fed or petted by anyone the owner has not allowed. Damage from another player is covered separately by the Animal Damage Protection setting below; a zombie, a fire or a vehicle can still kill a claimed animal.

Refuse damage from another PLAYER to a claimed animal - a weapon swing, a bullet, a thrown or placed explosive. Needs animal claims to be on. This refusal happens on the SERVER, so unlike the menu protections it holds even against a modified client. Environmental and accidental damage is deliberately left alone: a zombie, a predator, a fire, starvation and disease all still kill a claimed animal exactly as before. Two things a player can do are NOT covered and cannot be - running the animal over with a vehicle, and setting fire to it. The game gives a mod no way to see either coming, and this setting does not pretend otherwise.

Release a livestock claim after this many real days without the owner handling it. Lowering or enabling this restarts every clock. Set to 0 to never expire. Horses use their own separate setting. The clock is refreshed by the owner's own use; a friend on the allowed list using it does not keep the claim alive. (0-365)

Semicolon-separated list of padding values players can choose when claiming a safehouse. Example: 0;2;5;10 gives four options. Values are tile counts added around each side of the building footprint. Set to just 0 for no padding.
Allow players to claim a predefined grid area for custom-built structures that PZ doesn't recognize as buildings. Claims cannot overlap existing buildings, roads, or other claims.
Available grid sizes for custom land claims, comma-separated. (e.g. 10,20,30,40)

When on, a player whose server role matches one of the slots below uses that slot's safehouse and vehicle limits instead of the global Max Safehouse/Vehicle Claims. Off by default — when off, only the global limits apply and the slots are ignored.
When enabled, small garage and shed buildings (1-2 rooms) can be claimed if a residential building is nearby. Only applies when SafehouseAllowNonResidential is false.

When SafehouseAllowNonResidential is false, small buildings (like garages) that fail the room type check can still be claimed if a residential building is within this many tiles. Set to 0 to disable. (0-30)

Include horses in animal claims. Needs the master switch above, and needs the Horse mod (Workshop 3661336777) loaded on the server; with this on and the mod absent nothing changes, and the server log says so on boot. Turn this off and leave Include Livestock on to run a farm server where the herd is claimable and horses are free to anyone. A claimed horse also cannot be ridden, cannot have its saddlebags opened and cannot have its gear changed - and the mount refusal is the one protection here enforced by the server rather than by the player's own game.

Release a horse claim after this many real days without the owner riding it or using its saddlebags. Lowering or enabling this restarts every clock. Set to 0 to never expire. The clock is refreshed by the owner's own use; a friend on the allowed list riding it does not keep the claim alive. (0-365)

Include cows, chickens, pigs, sheep, deer and anything else the game or a mod adds. Needs the master switch above. Turn this off and leave Include Horses on to run a stable server where horses are claimable and wild animals are not.

How many non-horse animals one player may hold claims on at once. Separate from the horse limit, so a player can keep a couple of horses and a herd besides. Set to 0 to stop new livestock claims while leaving existing ones manageable. Role-based limits do not apply. (0-200)

How many horses one player may hold claims on at once. Separate from the livestock limit, so a player can keep a couple of horses and a herd besides. Set to 0 to stop new horse claims while leaving existing ones manageable. Role-based limits do not apply. (0-50)
Maximum number of safehouses a single player can own. (1-5)
Maximum number of vehicles a single player can claim. (0-10) Set to 0 to disable vehicle claiming entirely.

When enabled, players cannot claim safehouses, plots or custom claims inside areas an admin has drawn with the No-Claim Areas tool (Admin Panel > Zone Editor). Admins are not restricted, and players are never shown the areas: they get a generic refusal when they try. Turning this off keeps the drawn areas but stops enforcing them.

Allow players to mark out a land claim corner to corner: stand on one corner, pick Mark Plot Corner, walk to the opposite corner and claim the rectangle between. Separate from Custom Land Claims — you can run either, both, or neither. Off by default.

Largest total size of a plot claim, in tiles. Works with Max Side: this one stops very large plots, Max Side stops very long thin ones. The default 1600 is the same ceiling as a 40x40 custom claim. (1-10000)
Longest a plot claim may be along either edge, in tiles. Applies to both edges, since the player chooses the direction by which way they walk. (1-100)

Shortest a plot claim may be along either edge, in tiles. The default 1 permits one-tile strips, which are useful for fence lines and driveways — raise this if you would rather players could not claim a strip across a road or doorway. (1-100)

Minimum clearance, in tiles, between any claimed tile and a player spawn point. Measured edge-to-edge: no part of a claim (including padding) may come within this distance of a spawn point, or of the building containing one. Any positive value also prevents claiming the spawn structure itself. Set to 0 to disable spawn protection. (0-200)
Number of in-game days a player must wait between claiming safehouses. Set to -1 to use the vanilla SafehouseDaySurvivedToClaim setting. Set to 0 for no cooldown.

When enabled, the target player must accept an in-game prompt before being added to a safehouse claim. The target must be online; the invite expires after 60 seconds. Admins always bypass this check and add members instantly.
1 = Must contain ALL checked room types. 2 = Must contain AT LEAST ONE checked room type.
Building must contain a bathroom to be considered residential. Only applies when SafehouseAllowNonResidential is false.
Building must contain a bedroom to be considered residential. Only applies when SafehouseAllowNonResidential is false.
Building must contain a kitchen to be considered residential. Only applies when SafehouseAllowNonResidential is false.
Building must contain a living room to be considered residential. Only applies when SafehouseAllowNonResidential is false.

When enabled, players cannot claim safehouses inside zones tagged with the 'nosafehouse' property by the Phun Zones mod. Has no effect if Phun Zones is not installed. Lets server admins paint no-claim regions onto the map.

Exact name of a server role (built-in or custom) this slot applies to. Players with this role use the safehouse and vehicle limits set in this slot, overriding the global Max Safehouse/Vehicle Claims. Leave blank to disable this slot. Matching is case-insensitive.
Max safehouse claims for the role named in this slot. Only used when the role name above is filled in. (0-50)
Max vehicle claims for the role named in this slot. Only used when the role name above is filled in. (0-50)

Max vehicle claims for the role named in this slot. Only used when the role name above is filled in. (0-50)

Max safehouse claims for the role named in this slot. Only used when the role name above is filled in. (0-50)
Max vehicle claims for the role named in this slot. Only used when the role name above is filled in. (0-50)

Safehouses are automatically released after this many real days with no member activity. Any member logging in, being online, or being at the claim counts. Lowering or enabling this restarts existing clocks. Separately, the server option SafeHouseRemovalTime (hours) lets the game itself remove safehouses no member has stood inside; set it to 0 to leave expiry to this mod. Set to 0 to disable.
When enabled, claiming a building locks all doors and gives the player 2 safehouse keys. Players can lock/unlock doors from either side via context menu.
When enabled, claiming a trailer automatically gives the player a key for it. No skill or materials required.

Protect a claimed vehicle from other players. Two different things, with two different strengths. On the SERVER, and so proof against a modified client, it refuses four commands aimed at someone else's claimed vehicle: ramming it, smashing its windows, the damage a car takes from bodies it runs over, and deleting it outright - that last one vanilla lets any client do to any vehicle with no check at all. On the attacking player's own game only, it also stops a claimed vehicle being targeted by a melee swing. What is NOT stopped is gunfire: a bullet reaches the vehicle through a path with no hook a mod can reach, so a player who wants to shoot up a claimed car still can. Zombies, fire, ordinary wear and any crash caused by the owner or a member driving are untouched, and nothing is ever repaired or rolled back - a refused command simply does not run.

Claimed vehicles are automatically released after this many real days of owner inactivity. The owner logging in, being online, or using the vehicle counts; a friend on the allowed list does not. Lowering or enabling this restarts every clock rather than releasing claims already idle past the new value. Set to 0 to disable.
Minimum Electrical skill level required to craft a vehicle key. (0-10)
Allow players to craft vehicle keys from the right-click context menu. Requires tools (hacksaw, file set) and a steel bar quarter.
Minimum Mechanics skill level required to craft a vehicle key. (0-10)
